title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (reconstructed from this page and its neighbours; the axioms themselves are stated elsewhere). There is a set M of elementary 'places/figures' and a family 𝓕 of 'figures' F. Each F has a finite set F̃ ⊂ M of 'strata', partially ordered by X' ≤ X iff X' ≪ X. The relation Y ≪ X reads 'Y lies in the shadow (ombre) of X', roughly 'Y is a germ or stratum adherent to / infinitely near X'. For X ∈ M, Omb(X) = {Y ∈ M : Y ≪ X}. Multiomb(F) is a 'figure' of a second level, built from the shadows of the strata of F.

The observation on this page:
(1) The underlying set of Multiomb(F) is Omb(F) = |Multiomb F| := ⋃_{X∈F̃} Omb(X), i.e. the set of Y ∈ M with Y ≪ F.
(2) There is a canonical retraction φ_F : Omb(F) → F̃. It sends Y to the smallest stratum X ∈ F̃ with Y ≪ X, i.e. Y ∈ Omb X. On F̃ ⊂ Omb(F) it restricts to the identity. This retraction is exactly what defines the preorder on |Multiomb(F)|: an element of Omb F is ranked by the stratum it retracts to.
(3) A 'multi-figure' Φ is thus encoded as a set |Φ| together with a retraction onto a poset. For F, G ∈ 𝓕, Ψ = Multiomb(G) ≪ Φ = Multiomb(F) is defined to mean two things:
  - an inclusion |Ψ| ⊂ |Φ|, i.e. Omb G ⊂ Omb F;
  - an increasing map f : G̃ → F̃ making the square (1.48) commute: φ_F restricted to Omb G equals f ∘ φ_G.
(4) The next page proves this is equivalent to G ≪ F, with f(X) = the smallest element of F̃ dominating X. This completes the Proposition of the previous page: F ≪ G ⟺ Multiomb F ≪ Multiomb G.

Geometric picture: F̃ is the poset of strata of a stratified 'tame' figure, and Omb(F) is the set of germs near F. φ_F is a combinatorial shadow of a tubular-neighbourhood retraction onto strata (Thom–Mather control data), or of the 'entrance/exit' map to the stratification poset. The construction serves the 1986 attempt to axiomatize a tame topology ('analysis situs') purely combinatorially, through the incidence relation ≪.
errors: φ_F is well defined only if, for each Y ≪ F, the set {X ∈ F̃ : Y ≪ X} has a smallest element. This is an existence/uniqueness axiom not justified on this page; the next page's Corollary and 'nouveau postulat' remarks show Grothendieck was aware of it.

Commutativity of (1.48) needs a transitivity statement: the smallest dominating stratum in F̃ of the smallest dominating stratum in G̃ must equal the smallest dominating stratum in F̃. This is exactly the Corollary on the next page, which Grothendieck says may have to be assumed as a new postulate. The equivalence is therefore not yet proved here.

Equation numbering is inconsistent: the next page refers to commutation of '(1.42)' for this diagram and reuses (1.48) for a new notation. Page labels also run out of order (previous page shown as 29).

ideas.what: Canonical retraction from the shadow (set of germs/places adherent to F) onto the poset of strata of F, sending Y to the smallest stratum dominating it
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial analogue of a tubular-neighbourhood / control-data retraction onto strata; the map from a stratified space to its stratification poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970) for control data; Lurie / MacPherson for poset-stratified spaces and exit paths
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 discusses tame topology and tubular neighbourhoods qualitatively; this combinatorial form is not there

ideas.what: Encoding a 'figure of figures' (Multiomb) as a set with a retraction onto a poset, which induces a preorder; morphisms are inclusions plus increasing maps of posets commuting with the retractions
ideas.modern_name: maps of poset-stratified sets (stratified maps over a monotone map of posets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in stratified homotopy theory (Lurie HA Appendix A, Haine, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)

ideas.what: Characterizing G ≪ F (incidence of figures) by the existence of a commuting map of strata posets

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to axiomatize tame topology purely through an incidence relation ≪ ('shadow') on germs, with stratifications appearing as retractions Omb(F) → F̃. The required transitivity of 'smallest dominating stratum' is left as a possible new postulate. This purely combinatorial/order-theoretic axiomatics of stratified tame figures appears not to have been developed in the literature, where o-minimality took a different, model-theoretic route.
missed.quote: On a une rétraction canonique Omb(F) →φ_F F̃ ... associant à tout Y ∈ Omb F ... le plus petit X de F̃ parmi ceux satisfaisant Y ≪ X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a modest but concrete record of how Grothendieck intended 'tame topology' to be founded. It links his programme to poset-stratified spaces and exit-path categories, a connection historians and o-minimal/stratified-homotopy specialists have not documented from the manuscripts.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is foundational bookkeeping in an unpublished axiomatic tame-topology project. The ideas (retraction to a strata poset, stratified maps) are natural and essentially known in modern stratified theory. The interest is mainly historical: it shows the shape of Grothendieck's 1986 'analysis situs' axioms.
transcription_corrections: 'rétraction covariante' should probably read 'application croissante' (the next page says 'elle est évidemment croissante'; f : G̃ → F̃ is not a retraction).
'Multiomb' is the consistent name; the previous page's transcription 'Multicomb' is likely a misreading of 'Multiomb'.
In the definition of Omb(F) the struck symbol before Omb(X) is a crossed-out tilde/letter; the formula is Omb(F) = |Multiomb F| := ⋃_{X∈F̃} Omb(X).
'le plus petit élément de F̃ Y' likely reads 'le plus petit élément de F̃^Y' (notation F^X used on the next page for the set of elements of F̃ dominating X).
